title: Percy Severe, Cyril August and Earl Bostic
summary: Percy Severe left in 1936; Cyril August and Earl Bostic were the top altos, Bostic later in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: But you think Percy Severe came from Natchez?
That's where he supposed to be at home, Natchez, Mississippi.
Did he die or just leave here? Do you remember?

I never heard from Percy, it's been way back in 1936, and I haven't heard from Percy Severe since. There were a couple of musicians that have left here that killed D and stood here. And Cyril August, he was a, him and Cyril August and this guy here, oh, I can't think of him, he's still going strong on the alto horn, he plays a lot of alto, he makes a lot of recordings. Earl Bostic. Well, they was two top men's here during them times, Cyril August and Earl Bostic. Earl was working at the La Vida and Cyril was at the front with me. And they was two top alto players, you didn't know who was the best between the two. Well, Cyril left here, left his family, and he went to Pennsylvania, that's where he died, Pennsylvania. Earl Bostic, he settled out in Los Angeles. I saw him in 1958 too.
